questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew early that I wanted to go to Australia. I had been there before but due to covid I was forced to go home, and therefore I wanted to go back to get the full aussie experience. Furthermore, they have some very good universities and it is an english speaking country which makes it easier in classes and to get around etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's worth all of the time and money to go abroad. If you have the opportunity to go I would highly recommend it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy as we got a lot of emails about the first introduction week and the online portal which is like absalon (canvas) gave us all the information we needed for the school. Furthermore, it is always possible to write an email to the contact person from the university for any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it was great with the orientation days and activities for the exchange students and people were very helpful answering questions and helping.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at Scape cleveland which was recommended by the university. It was a room with 5 other roomies most of them were exchange students. It was pretty easy to find and arrange, however I wouldn't recommend staying there. It cost 10.000 DKK each month to stay there (it is generally expensive to live in Australia/Sydney). For the social reasons it was a really nice place, I had some good roomies and it was fun to live with people from around the world, and I also knew some others that lived there in the other apartments. Then it was also nice to have a room and bathroom for myself and I didn't have to share it with others (we only shared the kitchen and living room). However, it is not worth it to stay there for 10k a month with the condition of the apartment and the building and how the place is run by the manager. But near Redfern station there is Scape redfern which is really new and it has a rooftop terrace and kitchen, so I would recommend that over Scape cleveland.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived very close to campus, only a 10 min walk, so I think it is just as good staying off campus as on campus if it is close or you don't mind the transportation time. I also had some friends who lived further away but then they lived close to the beach which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to choose four courses which I found on the university's website. This was very time consuming and a bit hard, and I also had to change a course or two as my schedule didn't fit.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange contact person was there to help, however she was very busy as a lot of students send her emails everyday, so it sometimes took a while to get a response, but it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think it went fine and there was also some time after course start where it was possible to change to another course if it weren't the right one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to make an overview over the different courses you find that are interesting, to make it easier to decide.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took mostly 3000 level courses. I think that some of them were very challenging and the exams pretty hard (I also had 3 exams within 2 days), but I learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty much the same, however we had a bit more group work which I liked, but other than that there were also lectures and theoretical and lab exercises as at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Learning in outdoor education, Neuropharmacology, Human neuroscience in health and disease, and Biochemistry of Human disease.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend the course Learning in outdoor education. The teacher is very good and you get to go on some fields trips. It's a very reflective course and you learn a lot about the nature, culture etc. of australia. If you like learning about CNS and the brain I thought Neuropharmacology was very interesting from a pharmacology perspective and then the neuroscience course where you learn about the anatomy etc. However this course I also found very challenging.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were no plates, pots, pans, cutlery etc. at scape so I had to buy everything when I arrived.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I made a budget, where almost everything matched the expenses I had calculated from home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were different clubs at the university which hosted some events. Then there were also parties hosted by the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The parties at manning bar were always fun, so I would recommend those.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going to the blue mountains, I loved being there and hiking. On another weekend we rented a summer/ beach house and a car not far from Sydney in Callala Bay and it was so great to drive around and we went to the most beautiful beaches etc. I can also recommend going somewhere up the east coast, it is very easy to fly there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy. Of course everything is new in the beginning, but a lot is just like at home and people are so nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is easy to just talk to the other exchange students or danish students that you have met before, but I really think it is good to also try and be nice and friendly and get to know the local students e.g. in the same course as you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think Australia is a lot like Denmark, so it is easy to get around and talk to people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think people were very friendly and nice, and I think it was nice to see how much they talked about and respected the aboriginals and the culture from the indigenous people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take some courses that are interesting but also fun and different. Be outgoing and go to the social events. Enjoy your time there, the time passes by so fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to walk around campus before your first class, it is a big campus so you can easily get lost.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of new people, learn about the country and its culture and the new friendships I got.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I thought it was really difficult in the beginning, as I didn't knew anyone and I was all across the world from home. But after the first few hard days, everything were fine and I had a really nice stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
